summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for persistent right hip pain following a recent hospitalization. He had worsening pain despite high-dose prednisone and experienced a fall due to gait instability. Evaluation revealed no signs of septic joint, with normal CRP and negative joint fluid analysis. He underwent fluoroscopic-guided right hip joint aspiration and steroid injection, which improved his pain. Hyperkalemia was identified and treated, likely due to dietary potassium salt use. His condition stabilized with pain management, IV steroids, and physical therapy. He was discharged home ambulatory with a walker, on a prednisone taper, home medications, and plans to follow up with rheumatology to discuss starting Apremilast.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
